$comment: Cases both editors must judge alike, in the format of html.json: the Datastar attributes as the client reads them, their order on an element, the aliased prefix, filters written as values and what a computed may do.

cases.name: a media query is written with or without parentheses and quotes, as the reference allows

issues.message: data-match-media is a Datastar Pro attribute; it needs the Pro bundle.

cases.name: an indicator after the init whose request it is meant to show

issues.message: data-indicator comes after data-init, which starts its request as Datastar applies it, before the indicator exists, so the signal stays false. Put data-indicator first.

cases.name: a key written after a hyphen on an attribute that takes none

issues.message: data-text-foo is not a Datastar attribute. Did you mean data-text?
data-show-more is not a Datastar attribute. Did you mean data-show?
data-init-x is not a Datastar attribute. Did you mean data-init?

cases.name: a computed that changes signals or calls an action

issues.message: data-computed must not change signals, and this changes $b: Datastar runs it again each time a signal it reads changes. Use data-effect for a side effect.
data-computed must not call actions, and this calls @post: Datastar runs it again each time a signal it reads changes. Use data-effect for a side effect.
data-computed must not change signals, and this changes $e: Datastar runs it again each time a signal it reads changes. Use data-effect for a side effect.
data-computed must not change signals, and this changes $k: Datastar runs it again each time a signal it reads changes. Use data-effect for a side effect.
data-computed must not change signals, and this changes $m.n: Datastar runs it again each time a signal it reads changes. Use data-effect for a side effect.

cases.name: a signal filter written as an attribute's value, held to what filtered reads

issues.message: include takes a regular expression or a string, and 5 is a number, so Datastar throws a TypeError as it matches a signal.
A signal filter has only include and exclude, so Datastar ignores exclde. Did you mean exclude?
data-on-signal-patch-filter takes an object of include and exclude, and 'counter' is a string, so Datastar reads no filter from it.
data-json-signals takes an object of include and exclude, and null is none, so Datastar throws a TypeError as it reads it.
